prompt:
Faults of the last attempt, to avoid this time:
- Cells 1, 2, 3 and 5: the porch roof was drawn as a box sticking out below the outline's thick bottom edge, about 8–15 px past it. Nothing may be drawn outside an outline. Each roof fills its outline exactly, edge to edge, and the porch is a small lean-to roof drawn INSIDE the outline, along the thick bottom edge, its bottom edge on the outline's bottom edge.
- Cell 3: drawn about 9% too wide, past both side edges.
- Every chimney was drawn about 1.8 m across, three times its true 0.6 m: at this scale a chimney is a small square a third of a car's width; draw it about a third of the size it was. Skylights likewise smaller, about 0.8 × 1 m.

Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 6 building outlines seen from above, in a 3×2 grid on a flat magenta background. The second is finished art from the same game, to match in style only — not its layout, shapes, colours or the size of its details.

Make one image with exactly the same 3×2 layout as the first image. Inside each outline, draw the roof of the building described for that cell below, as a top-down sprite for a 2D city game.

Shape comes first. Before painting a cell, trace its outline exactly, then paint only inside the traced border:
- Keep every outline's proportions: match each one's width and height. Each cell's proportion is given below; check it. Never make an outline squarer, shorter or fatter.
- Every edge is straight and square to the others. Never slant, skew or taper an edge to show perspective. An outline built of several rectangles (an L, a T, a stepped block) is followed corner by corner.
- Draw nothing outside the outline: no eaves, steps, porches, canopies, ramps or shadows past it. A porch or an entrance canopy is drawn inside the outline at its bottom edge. Inside a roof there is no magenta at all.

Scale is the second rule, and it is strict. Every size below is true metres, width × depth, and every detail is drawn at its true size against them. These buildings stand beside cars 4 m long and 1.8 m wide; keep that in mind for every detail. True sizes:
- house: a brick chimney about 0.6 × 0.6 m; roof tile courses or corrugations about 0.25 m apart, fine and close; a skylight about 0.8 × 1 m; a dormer about 1.5–2 m wide; a porch roof about 1.5–2 m deep.
- No detail is bigger than its true size. When in doubt, draw it smaller and keep fewer of them. A large roof has many small details, never a few huge ones.

Rules for every cell:
- Look straight down (orthographic). No perspective, no walls seen from the side, no tilt, no ground, no plants, no cars, no people.
- The thick bottom edge of each outline is the street front, where the entrance is. The top edge is the back.
- A gabled roof shows its ridge as one line with the two slopes shaded differently; a lean-to roof is one slope with no ridge; a flat roof has a parapet round its edge.
- Style: match the style image. Clean, flat-shaded cartoon game art, bold dark outlines, muted natural colours, simple readable details, soft light from the top-left.
- Outside the roofs, keep the background flat pure magenta #FF00FF. No text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, grid lines or frames anywhere.

Cells, left to right, top to bottom:

Row 1
1. 16.1 × 6.3 m (2.6× wider than deep, a thin strip) — detached family house, gabled roof of grey corrugated asbestos-cement slate, a chimney and a skylight, small porch roof over the door
2. 16.1 × 7.7 m (2.1× wider than deep, corners widely rounded) — detached family house, hipped roof of dark grey bitumen shingles, a chimney and a skylight, small porch roof over the door, its corners rounded in wide curves
3. 6.3 × 10.5 m (1.7× deeper than wide) — small single-storey cottage, gabled roof of brown metal tiles, one brick chimney, a lean-to porch on the street side, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall, its ridge running from the street to the back

Row 2
4. 14.7 × 10.5 m (1.4× wider than deep) — detached family house, gabled roof of grey corrugated asbestos-cement slate, a chimney and a skylight, small porch roof over the door
5. 18.2 × 7.7 m (2.4× wider than deep) — detached family house, hipped roof of red clay tiles, a chimney and a skylight, small porch roof over the door
6. 9.8 × 11.9 m (1.2× deeper than wide) — detached family house, gabled roof of green-painted sheet metal, a chimney and a skylight, small porch roof over the door, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall, its ridge running from the street to the back
